messages:
jen: Kicking off POC for Nomad Insurance — they ran a sustained soak and we saw intermittent peak jitter around bursts. Sharing the raw load run and a few asks: can we confirm how routing fallback behaves under saturation? Also need pricing for sustained 500 QPS for a month (they care about predictable cost), and security question about customer KMS/HSM for Private deployment. Attached: link to run artifacts.

alex: Thanks. What was the exact load profile (ramp, sustain, spikes)? and which model variant were you running?

jen: Ramp 5m -> sustain 30m at 500 qps, plus 5 spikes to 1.2k for 30s. Model: openchat-medium-v1 (quantized). Artifacts: https://files.redwood/test-runs/nomad-0316.zip

maria: Quick read — p50 looks fine but p95 spikes during the 1.2k surges. My guess: prefix cache miss amplification + cross-AZ routing fallback. For a prospect wanting predictability, recommend Dedicated with region affinity + small burst pool. Also set cache TTL to 60s for hot prompts.

siva: Confirming behavior: smart routing will try same AZ pool, then fallback to same-region compatible variant if capacity low, then cross-region if policy allows. That fallback explains latency jumps. We can force no-cross-region fallback for SLA-sensitive tests.

maria: Also try enabling prefix/KV cache on client side (we saw a 20-30% token save during our internal runs).

alex: Can you paste the reproduce commands? I'd like to rerun locally with same seed.

siva: Use vegeta script we used for the last sales POC. Example:

```
cat profile.json | vegeta attack -rate=500 -duration=35m | vegeta report
```

profile.json includes ramp annotations and spikes (we can share). If you want to force fallback, add header `x-redwood-routing: prefer-local;fallback=none` in the request.

ops-bot: Deployment test runner finished: 1768509805 - canary config applied to dedicated-pool-42 for 10m. Results posted to /runs/1768509805.

jen: Pricing ask from customer: committed monthly or PAYG? They want to compare predictable cost vs spot.

sam: Ballpark: For Dedicated reserved we typically quote a committed instance bundle that covers ~500 qps sustained for that model at $18k/mo (includes baseline throughput and SLA). PAYG for hosted (wide) would be ~ $0.012 per generated token — rough, depends on token length; over a month that scales with usage and can exceed the reserved price for sustained loads. We can draft a formal quote.

alex: Thanks Sam. We should include burst add-on pricing for those 1.2k spikes (they want acceptance criteria).

maria: For acceptance criteria: p95 < 250ms for sustain, <500ms for short spikes (30s) with no errors. If they require stricter, need higher commit or more regional pools.

jen: Security questionnaire: they asked if we support customer-managed KMS/HSM in hosted.

sec-bot: Short answer: customer-managed KMS is supported for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with HSM integrations via our enterprise package. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with our KMS; can discuss dedicated keying via an enterprise contract. See: https://redwood.docs/security/kms-integration.

jen: OK. Next steps: 1) Alex to rerun with header forcing no-cross-region fallback and post results. 2) Maria to prepare recommendation doc (Dedicated config + cache + burst pool) and draft acceptance SLAs. 3) Sam to prepare a 1-page committed vs PAYG pricing compare. 4) Sec to give short note for customer sec questionnaire.

alex: On it — I'll post a short results thread by EOD PST.

maria: I'll assemble config snippets and expected perf numbers.

jen: Great — we'll loop in the customer after we have the adjusted run. :thumbsup:
